taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000078 Defective-State Carryforward Failure was tested because the user reports unwanted assistant-generated framing becoming sticky across deletion or thread movement, but the preserved occurrence does not establish a discrete receiving-side continuation in which inherited defective state was then treated as a sufficient basis for material reasoning or execution without revalidation, repair, quarantine, rollback or reset. VIGIL-FC-000006 Control-Plane Authority Crossover was also considered, but the exact memory or derivation mechanism is not documented and the evidence does not establish that generated content was promoted into policy, configuration, routing, permissions, checkpoint, memory-policy or other operative control-plane state. The current taxonomy therefore does not justify a mapping from persistence language alone.

Primary classification changed: no — remains unclassified. Existing classifications retained: none. External-assessment material was checked where present; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5. The newer continuity class narrows the relevant boundary, but the remaining problem is occurrence-specific mechanism evidence rather than a demonstrated class fit.
